name: Generative Agents (Memory Stream + Reflection + Planning)
executive_summary: Give an agent a long-term memory stream, periodically synthesize it into reflections, and retrieve relevant memories dynamically to inform planning — an architecture for believable, persistent agent behavior.
description: Distinct from Reflexion's episodic retry-memory: this is a standing architecture for agents that operate continuously over long horizons, not just across retries at one task. Three components work together — a memory stream recording every observation in natural language, a reflection process that periodically synthesizes recent memories into higher-level insights, and a retrieval function that scores stored memories by recency, importance, and relevance to pull the right context into each planning decision. Demonstrated in a sandbox environment where 25 agents exhibited emergent believable behaviors (planning a party, spreading information, forming relationships) purely from this memory/reflection/planning loop, without any of it being scripted.
when_to_use: Building an agent that needs to operate coherently over a long horizon with many interactions, where relevant context from far in the past needs to resurface at the right moment (not just the most recent turns).
when_not_to_use: Short, single-session tasks where a standing memory architecture is pure overhead — Reflexion's lighter episodic memory or plain context suffices.
known_pitfalls: Memory retrieval quality (the recency/importance/relevance scoring function) is a single point of failure — poorly tuned retrieval surfaces the wrong memories at the wrong time, degrading planning quality without an obvious error signal.

primary_source.authors: Park, O'Brien, Cai, Morris, Liang, Bernstein
primary_source.title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
